Title: Mapping Global Trade in Fakes 2025
Summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. OECD–EUIPO analysis estimates that counterfeit and pirated goods represented up to 2.3% of global trade in 2021. Published in 2025 but based on 2021 customs seizure data, it provides an updated international enforcement benchmark rather than a current Australian market estimate. Strategic implication: explore customs intelligence partnerships and risk-based SME support; do not use these global figures to extrapolate Australia's counterfeit market or validate the 2022 growth assumption.

Title: Amazon's Trustworthy Shopping Experience Report 2025
Summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem; Amplify Australian IP. Amazon reports that proactive controls blocked more than 99.9% of suspected infringing listings before brand owners needed to report them, and that more than 15 million counterfeit products were identified, seized and disposed of during 2025. Its tools combine brand registration, infringement reporting, product serialisation and direct removal capabilities. Strategic implication: examine platform partnerships and practical SME onboarding support, while treating company-reported results as platform-specific evidence rather than independent measures of Australian coverage.

Title: UK Intellectual Property Office mediation service
Summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. The UK IPO offers mediation covering patents, trade marks, designs, copyright, trade secrets and related commercial matters, including online sessions. Both parties must agree to participate. Strategic implication: a comparator for affordable post-registration dispute support, including referral partnerships, online delivery and transparent pricing; evaluate suitability, settlement outcomes and participation barriers rather than assuming mediation can replace enforcement. The publication date is the guidance page's original publication date, not the commencement date of every current service feature.

Title: Australian IP Report 2026: productivity and income research
Summary: Territories: Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. IP Australia reports that businesses registering their first trade mark experienced an average 16% increase in sales per worker compared with equivalent businesses on similar growth paths without protection; first patent grants were associated with a 15% increase in overall efficiency. Strategic implication: develop evidence-based outreach linking suitable IP protection to business outcomes, while avoiding promises that registration alone will produce these gains for individual SMEs.

Title: Australian IP Report 2025: examination timing and commercialisation
Summary: Territories: Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. The report discusses research indicating that small innovators engaging with IP early can benefit from influencing examination timing, with implications for innovation, commercialised products and lifetime IP value. Strategic implication: investigate customer-controlled timing and guidance that align protection with experimentation, funding and market entry, rather than treating faster examination as universally preferable. Publication year: 2025; an exact publication date was not established from the retrieved source.

Title: EUIPO SME Fund 2025
Summary: Territories: Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. EUIPO reports that the sixth edition of its SME Fund launched on 3 February 2025 through collaboration with the European Commission and European Union Intellectual Property Network, providing financial support for SME intellectual property protection. Strategic implication: examine targeted financial assistance delivered through partner networks as a comparator for reducing Australian SME cost barriers. Assess additional uptake, application quality and commercial usefulness rather than registration volumes alone. The date records the announcement's publication.

Title: UK IP Advance grant funding
Summary: Territories: Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. UK government guidance identifies IP Advance as a scheme supporting innovative SMEs with intellectual property, including copyright, designs, trade marks and patents. Strategic implication: examine the scheme as a comparator for assistance spanning different IP assets rather than a single registration pathway, and investigate eligibility, delivery partners and outcomes before considering Australian adaptation.

Title: WIPO IP Finance Dialogue 2025: The Value of Intangible Assets
Summary: Territories: Amplify Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. WIPO's dialogue brought together issues of IP valuation, recognition, disclosure and access to capital, highlighting the need to build lender and investor trust in intangible assets. Strategic implication: explore common IP information templates, valuation literacy and partnerships with financiers and valuation professionals; distinguish an asset's estimated commercial value from its acceptability as loan collateral. The date is the dialogue date rather than a verified webpage publication date.

Title: UK Intellectual Property Office Corporate Plan 2025 to 2026
Summary: Territories: Amplify Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem. The plan identifies engagement with industry to help innovative SMEs leverage IP assets to access finance and commits to publishing an IP finance annual report. Strategic implication: an institutional comparator for an IP office extending beyond registration through evidence development and finance-sector engagement, without assuming that the office must itself become a lender or valuation provider. Publication year: 2025; an exact publication date was not established from the retrieved source.

Title: Australian IP Report 2026: research programme and IP First Response
Summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Cultivate our ecosystem; Empower others. The research programme records progress during 2025 on IP First Response, a pilot digital service assisting both SMEs facing suspected infringement and businesses accused of infringement. Strategic implication: design post-registration support around both sides of disputes, with proportionate triage and referral pathways rather than rights-holder enforcement alone. This is evidence of service development, not proof of reduced dispute costs or improved outcomes. Publication year: 2026; an exact chapter publication date was not established.

Title: Australian IP Report 2026: Indigenous business research partnerships
Summary: Territories: Cultivate our ecosystem; Revisit our purpose; Amplify Australian IP. IP Australia's research programme identifies collaboration with the University of Melbourne's Dilin Duwa Centre for Indigenous Business Leadership to examine the commercial value of trade marks for Indigenous businesses and the potential economic role of trade marks containing Indigenous Knowledge. Strategic implication: use Indigenous-led research partnerships to test whose value is recognised and how services support Indigenous economic participation, without reducing cultural value to registration or financial metrics. Publication year: 2026; an exact chapter publication date was not established.

Title: WIPO Treaty on Intellectual Property, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
Summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. Adopted on 24 May 2024, the treaty establishes a patent disclosure framework concerning genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. WIPO explains that the disclosure requirement operates upon entry into force following ratification by 15 contracting parties. Strategic implication: examine provenance information, applicant guidance and engagement with Indigenous Peoples; do not describe adoption alone as creating an operative Australian disclosure obligation or comprehensive Indigenous Knowledge protection. The date is the treaty's adoption date.

Title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 2: Copyrightability
Summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Empower others; Amplify Australian IP. The US Copyright Office concludes that generative AI outputs can receive copyright protection where a human determines sufficient expressive elements, but not merely through providing prompts; AI assistance does not itself disqualify a work. Strategic implication: distinguish human contribution, ownership and protectability when developing AI-related guidance and assessing commercial IP value. This is a US legal-policy position, not a statement of Australian copyright law.

Title: IP Australia Strategic Corporate Plan 2026–27
Summary: Territories: Revisit our purpose; Cultivate our ecosystem; Empower others. IP Australia's announcement identifies AI governance and accountability, First Nations engagement and economic empowerment, and improved services, education and guidance as priorities. Strategic implication: use these commitments as a current alignment framework for horizon initiatives, particularly responsible AI-enabled assistance, inclusive service design and partnership proposals. The date records the announcement's publication.

Title: Australian IP Report 2026: structural shifts in international IP activity
Summary: Territories: Protect Australian IP; Empower others; Cultivate our ecosystem. IP Australia reports that Australian resident trade mark filings increased 15% in 2025, applications originated from 138 locations, and Australian resident patent filings increased 9%, alongside declining US-linked international patent collaboration and increasing Chinese-origin activity in applied and industrial technologies. Strategic implication: reassess priority markets, overseas protection guidance and partner networks using changing filing patterns; filings indicate system use, not infringement incidence or proof of commercial success.
